title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is an isolated leaf. The neighbouring pages are an unrelated Bourbaki-style draft on holomorphic functions. The fragment is about supersingular elliptic curves, or rank-2 Dieudonné crystals, with a CM structure by the imaginary quadratic field Q(sqrt(-p)), described in crystalline terms. It begins mid-argument: some data over an open set U_ξ (presumably of a moduli or arithmetic base, not visible here) is equivalent to giving a triple (M_0, o, i). After the corrections the triple reads as follows.

- M is a (Dieudonné) crystal over F_{p^2}. In a supersingular situation this is the crystal of a supersingular elliptic curve, or of its p-divisible group.
- o is an order acting on M. In context this is presumably a maximal order of the quaternion algebra B_{p,∞}, i.e. End(E) of a supersingular curve.
- i : R → o is an embedding, where R is the ring of integers of Q[T]/(T^2+p) = Q(sqrt(-p)).

Grothendieck then reformulates. Giving i amounts to giving a descent M_0 of M from F_{p^2} to F_p whose (p-linear, relative) Frobenius satisfies F^2 + p = 0. This is the familiar fact that an F_p-rational supersingular curve has Frobenius π with π^2 = -p (trace 0, p > 3). So Z[π] = Z[sqrt(-p)] ⊂ End_{F_p}(E). Equivalently, an F_p-structure is the same as an embedding of the 'Frobenius order' into the endomorphisms.

He then lists the conditions a functorial construction on such data must satisfy:
(i) compatibility with isomorphisms of triples (M_0, o, i) ≅ (M_0', o', i');
(ii) compatibility with twisting by an invertible R-module P_0, via Serre's tensor construction M ↦ M ⊗_R P_0, using the canonical isomorphism det_Z P_0 ≅ Z. This identification is what makes twisting preserve the determinant, i.e. the polarization / Weil pairing.

The twisting in (ii) is the action of Pic(R) on F_p-rational supersingular curves with CM by R, the Deuring–Waterhouse class-group action. Overall, the page appears to be setting up a 'motivic Galois' or descent datum for CM motives of weight 1 at p ramified in the CM field. Very likely it serves an analysis of supersingular reduction in a theory of motives with complex multiplication, or of the motivic Galois group over F_p.
errors: The text identifies R, the ring of integers of Q(sqrt(-p)), with what is generated by the Frobenius of an F_p-descent (F^2+p=0). Frobenius generates only Z[sqrt(-p)]. For p ≡ 3 mod 4, R = Z[(1+sqrt(-p))/2] strictly contains this. So 'giving i' and 'giving an F_p-descent with F^2+p=0' are not equivalent without extra care: R-action versus Z[π]-action, the 'surface/floor' distinction of Delfs–Galbraith. The page glosses over this.

Notation is inconsistent because of the corrections. M_0 is first introduced as the crystal over F_{p^2}, then renamed M, and M_0 becomes its descent to F_p. The parenthetical 'sans opération sur M qui descend à F_p' is ambiguous.

ideas.what: Supersingular elliptic curves over F_p (Frobenius π^2 = -p) correspond to embeddings of Z[sqrt(-p)] or R into the quaternion endomorphism order, phrased via Dieudonné crystals and descent from F_{p^2} to F_p
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence / F_p-rational supersingular curves and optimal embeddings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941); Waterhouse (1969); Delfs–Galbraith (2016) for the F_p-rational case

ideas.what: Use of crystals (Dieudonné modules) as the linear-algebra incarnation of the p-adic realization of a motive
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (crystals, 1966; Barsotti–Tate groups, Montréal 1970), Berthelot, Mazur–Messing
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (1974)

ideas.what: Compatibility with twisting by invertible R-modules P_0, using det_Z P_0 ≅ Z
ideas.modern_name: Serre tensor construction; class group action on CM curves (as later used in CSIDH-type settings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre/Shimura–Taniyama (CM theory); Waterhouse 1969; Castryck et al. 2018 (CSIDH)

missed.claim: A fragmentary set-up of crystalline data for CM-by-Q(sqrt(-p)) supersingular objects over F_p, with axioms (isomorphism invariance, Pic(R)-twisting) presumably intended to characterize some functorial construction. The purpose (the 'données /U_ξ') is not visible on this page. It is consistent with known Deuring/Waterhouse theory and is unfinished.
missed.quote: compatibilité avec twist par un module inversible P_0 sous R, compte tenu de l'isom. can. det_Z P_0 ≃ Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest. It shows Grothendieck treating the F_p-rational supersingular class-group action (now central in CSIDH isogeny cryptography) crystallinely around 1965-70. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short, unfinished fragment of standard CM / supersingular theory in crystalline language. It is mildly interesting historically as an early crystalline treatment of Pic(Z[sqrt(-p)]) twisting on F_p-supersingular data, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: Opening probably reads 'Ceci est équivalent [à] la donnée des 2 données /U_ξ' rather than 'Je est équivalent'.
Q[T]/(T^2+p): the Q appears written over a crossed-out Z.
After corrections, M (not M_0) is the crystal over F_{p^2}, and M_0 is its descent to F_p. The crossed-out text is 'M_0 ⊗_{F_p} F_{p^2}' and 'telles que R opère sur M_0'.
'inclusion' is written 'inclusion' (or 'injection'); 'compte tenu de l'isom. can.' is correct.
'Les conditions sont' is plausibly 'Les conditions sur ...' (incomplete), followed by the list.
